request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Redacted]
Sex: Female
Age: 29 Years
Hospital: Orašje County Hospital (Bosnia and Herzegovina)
Admission Date: [Redacted]
Discharge Date: [Redacted]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
A 29-year-old female was admitted to the Department of Surgery with a history of recurrent colicky right upper quadrant abdominal pain. The patient was diagnosed as having multiple gallstones within the gallbladder on abdominal ultrasonography. Routine hematological and biochemical test results were normal. The patient underwent elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, and there were no complications during the procedure, or postoperatively. The patient was discharged on the third postoperative day. 

Pathology Report:
Histologically, microscopic slides from the gallbladder body showed that almost the entire cylindrical epithelium of the mucosa was missing. There was a moderate mixed inflammatory cell infiltrate in the submucosa, and the muscular layer was slightly hypertrophic, which is consistent with chronic cholecystitis. The most unusual feature of the slide from the body of the gallbladder was the presence of large dilated vessels within the muscular layer extending into the submucosa and mucosa. The appearance of angiodysplasia of the gallbladder and its endothelial lining was confirmed immunohistochemically using CD34, CD31, and podoplanin (D2-40) monoclonal antibodies. 

Follow-up:
The patient remained healthy at 6-year follow-up. 

Summary:
The patient, a 29-year-old woman, underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy for multiple gallstones within the gallbladder. The histopathological findings revealed chronic cholecystitis with the unusual feature of angiodysplasia of the gallbladder. There were no complications during the procedure, and the patient was discharged on the third postoperative day. The patient remained healthy at the 6-year follow-up.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is gallstones in the gallbladder with chronic cholecystitis, which falls under category K80 (cholelithiasis).

- **Chapter (K):** The episode was an elective admission for symptomatic gallbladder disease, which belongs to the digestive system chapter.
- **Category (80):** The patient was admitted for recurrent biliary colic due to multiple gallstones, and laparoscopic cholecystectomy was performed. Histology confirmed chronic cholecystitis. Gallstones with cholecystitis are classified within K80 (cholelithiasis), not K81 (cholecystitis without stones). The full code would be K80.1, calculus of gallbladder with other cholecystitis.
- **Angiodysplasia:** The gallbladder angiodysplasia was an incidental histopathological finding, likely K82.8. It did not occasion the admission, so it is at most an additional diagnosis.

CODE: K80
